assumption: Elliott–Halberstam conjecture (level of distribution of primes)
title: Break the 5/8 barrier for primes with triply well-factorable weights
W: The primes are known to be evenly spread over residue classes, on average over moduli up to x^{5/8}, if the average is weighted by triply well-factorable weights. Push the exponent past 5/8, or show the dispersion method cannot.
M: Let $\theta^*$ be the supremum of $\theta$ such that for every triply well-factorable sequence $\lambda_q$ supported on $q\le x^{\theta}$ and every fixed $a\ne0$: $\sum_{q\le x^\theta,(q,a)=1}\lambda_q\big(\pi(x;q,a)-\pi(x)/\varphi(q)\big)\ll_{A,a} x(\log x)^{-A}$. Known: $\theta^*\ge 5/8$ (Pascadi 2025; earlier $3/5$ Maynard, $66/107$ Lichtman). Prove $\theta^*>5/8$.
why: Exponents past 1/2 are the only unconditional form of Elliott–Halberstam usable in sieves; each step (4/7, 3/5, 66/107, 5/8) improved twin-prime upper bounds and Goldbach-type results. Pascadi states that 5/8 seems to be the limit of current Kloosterman/large-sieve technology in every sieve-relevant setting, so passing it would need a new idea, and a proven barrier would be informative too.
status_notes: EH open. Level beyond 1/2 known only for well-factorable weights: BFI 4/7; Maynard 3/5; Lichtman 66/107 (5/8 under Selberg's eigenvalue conjecture); Pascadi 2025 reached 5/8 unconditionally (arXiv 2505.00653), noting quadruply well-factorable weights do not help.

assumption: Elliott–Halberstam conjecture (level of distribution of primes)
title: Improve H_1 <= 12 under EH alone
W: Assuming Elliott–Halberstam, Maynard's sieve gives infinitely many pairs of primes at distance at most 12. The generalized conjecture GEH gives 6. Lower 12 using EH alone.
M: Let $H_1=\liminf_{n}(p_{n+1}-p_n)$. Assuming EH (level $\theta=1-\varepsilon$ for all $\varepsilon>0$, for the von Mangoldt function only, not GEH), prove $H_1\le 10$, or prove that no Selberg/Maynard-type sieve weight using EH alone can give $H_1<12$.
why: This isolates how much EH alone, as opposed to its generalization to Dirichlet convolutions, can do for prime gaps. Either answer clarifies the logical strength of the hypothesis most used in conditional prime-gap results.
status_notes: Polymath8b (Res. Math. Sci. 2014): H_1<=246 unconditionally, <=12 under EH (Maynard), <=6 under GEH; the parity barrier makes the GEH triple result optimal for pure sieves. I found no improvement of 12 under plain EH.

assumption: Cramér random model / Granville refinement; Hardy–Littlewood k-tuples
title: Interval-sieve extremal bounds behind the Banks–Ford–Tao gap prediction
W: Banks, Ford and Tao showed that a random sieve model of the primes predicts the largest prime gap below x is about g(ξ log²x), where g is controlled by an extremal sieve quantity W_y. W_y is the fewest survivors in [0,y] after one residue class is removed for each prime up to √(y/log y). Narrow the bounds on W_y.
M: Let $W_y=\min_{(a_p)}\#\{n\in[0,y]: n\not\equiv a_p \pmod p\ \forall p\le (y/\log y)^{1/2}\}$. Banks–Ford–Tao (Invent. 2023, eq. (1.12)) prove $(4+o(1))\frac{y\log_2 y}{\log^2 y}\le W_y\le \frac{y}{\log y}+O(\frac{y\log_2y}{\log^2y})$ (the upper bound is believed to be close to the truth). Prove $W_y\ge c\,y/\log y$ for some absolute $c>0$ (no such bound is known), or construct residue choices giving $W_y=o(y/\log y)$.
why: This is the one unknown quantity standing between the Cramér/Granville models and a sharp conjecture for large gaps (constant ξ=2e^{-γ}). A lower bound of order y/log y would make the prediction G(x)≍log²x unconditional within the model, and would improve Iwaniec's J(w)≪w² for Jacobsthal's function. A construction giving o(y/log y) would show the model predicts gaps of larger order than log²x.
status_notes: BFT (Invent. Math. 2023) model predicts G(x) between g((ξ∓ε)log²x), ξ=2e^{-γ}; they pose improving (1.12) as Open Problem 1; Landau–Siegel zeros would force liminf W_y/(y/log y)=0 (their Thm 2.2). Jacobsthal: J(w)≪w² (Iwaniec) still best upper.

assumption: Montgomery pair correlation / GUE random-matrix model for zeta zeros
title: Push the GRH lower bound for Montgomery's F(alpha) beyond alpha = 1
W: Montgomery's function F(α) is known only for |α|≤1 (on RH). Under GRH for Dirichlet L-functions, Goldston–Gonek–Özlük–Snyder proved F(α) ≥ 3/2−|α|−ε on 1≤|α|≤3/2, while the conjecture says F(α)=1 there. Improve this lower bound.
M: Assume GRH for all Dirichlet $L$-functions. Prove that for some $\delta>0$ and all $\alpha\in[1,1+\delta]$, $\liminf_{T\to\infty}F(\alpha,T)\ge \tfrac32-\alpha+\delta$, or prove $\liminf_T \int_{1}^{3/2}F(\alpha,T)\,d\alpha>1/8$ (the value forced by the GGOS bound).
why: The range |α|>1 is where the GUE prediction meets Hardy–Littlewood prime-pair correlations, and also where the Alternative Hypothesis (half-integer spacings) departs from GUE. Any improvement under GRH alone would be the first progress past GGOS (2000) and would constrain exotic zero distributions.
status_notes: PCC open; F(α) asymptotic known only for |α|≤1 under RH (Montgomery, Goldston–Montgomery). GGOS (PLMS 2000) gives F(α)≥3/2−|α|−ε on [1,3/2) under GRH. 2025 work (Baluyot–Goldston–Suriajaya–Turnage-Butterbaugh) derives F under AH as a sawtooth plus deltas; AH is still not refuted.

assumption: Montgomery pair correlation / GUE random-matrix model for zeta zeros
title: Do GRH and Elliott–Halberstam together refute the Alternative Hypothesis?
W: The Alternative Hypothesis says normalized gaps between zeta zeros are almost all near half-integers. It contradicts GUE, but no proven hypothesis is known to rule it out. Decide whether GRH plus Elliott–Halberstam (strong statements about primes, not zeros) is incompatible with it.
M: Let AH be the hypothesis of Baluyot–Goldston–Suriajaya–Turnage-Butterbaugh (arXiv 2508.10857), under which (with RH) $F(\alpha)$ has an explicit sawtooth-plus-delta limit for all real $\alpha$. Determine whether GRH for Dirichlet $L$-functions together with EH (or GEH) implies $\neg$AH. Equivalently, compute the strongest constraints on $\int_0^b F(\alpha,T)\,d\alpha$ for $b\in(1,2]$ that follow from GRH+EH, and check them against the AH prediction.
why: AH must be disproved to rule out Landau–Siegel zeros by the Conrey–Iwaniec spacing route, yet it is consistent with everything known about correlations (Lagarias–Rodgers). Showing that standard prime hypotheses kill AH, or that they are compatible with it, would sharply separate what prime-side hypotheses can say about the fine structure of zeros.
status_notes: Lagarias–Rodgers (QJM 2020) built a point process satisfying AH and all known band-limited correlation constraints. BGST 2025 compute F(α) under RH+AH. I found no paper relating EH/GEH to AH; Goldston–Montgomery-type equivalences link F(α), |α|>1, to prime variance in short intervals, not to APs.

assumption: Katz–Sarnak random-matrix symmetry types for low-lying zeros (GRH-based)
title: One-level density of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions beyond support (−2,2)
W: Under GRH, the low-lying zeros of L(s,χ_d) for quadratic characters are known to follow the symplectic random-matrix law only for test functions whose Fourier transform is supported in (−2,2). Go beyond 2.
M: For the family of real primitive characters $\chi_{8d}$, $d$ odd squarefree, $X<d\le 2X$, and even Schwartz $\phi$ with $\operatorname{supp}\hat\phi\subset(-\sigma,\sigma)$, prove under GRH that $\frac1{|\mathcal F|}\sum_d\sum_{\gamma_d}\phi\!\big(\gamma_d\frac{\log X}{2\pi}\big)\to\int\phi(x)\big(1-\frac{\sin 2\pi x}{2\pi x}\big)dx$ for some $\sigma>2$.
why: Support beyond 2 is the classic test of the symplectic prediction in its non-trivial range and would give better nonvanishing proportions for L(1/2,χ_d). For the averaged family of all Dirichlet characters, Drappeau–Pratt–Radziwiłł got past 2 unconditionally (to 2+50/1093) using large-sieve and dispersion input. The question is whether analogous input exists for the thinner quadratic family.
status_notes: Özlük–Snyder: support (−2,2) under GRH for quadratic family; Rubinstein for n-level. Drappeau–Pratt–Radziwiłł (ANT 2023): beyond 2 (to 2+50/1093) for all primitive characters with conductor in [Q/2,Q]. I found no extension past 2 for the quadratic family; ratios-conjecture computations predict the answer.

title: Lower the exponent 1/2 in Pasten's subexponential abc bound
W: Unconditionally, abc is known only in very weak forms. Pasten (2024) proved that if a ≤ c^{1−η} then log c ≤ η^{-1} exp(κ√(log R · log log R)), with R = rad(abc). abc predicts log c ≤ (1+ε) log R + O(1). Replace the square root by any smaller power of log R.
M: For coprime $a+b=c$ with $R=\mathrm{rad}(abc)$, Pasten (Invent. Math. 2024, Thm 1.4) proves: if $a\le c^{1-\eta}$ then $\log c\le \eta^{-1}\exp\big(\kappa\sqrt{\log R\,\log_2 R}\big)$; and $\log c\le q\exp(\kappa\sqrt{\log R\log_2R})$ with $q=\min\{P(a),P(b),P(c)\}$. Prove either statement with $\exp((\log R)^{\theta})$ for some fixed $\theta<1/2$, or $\exp(O(\sqrt{\log R}))$.
why: Pasten's Shimura-curve plus linear-forms method gave the first improvement on Stewart–Yu in two decades and the first superlinear-in-log₂ bound for P(n²+1). The exponent 1/2 comes from a single balancing step, so it is a natural target. Lowering it would measure how far the modular method can approach abc without relying on IUT.
status_notes: abc open; Mochizuki's IUT claim is disputed (Scholze–Stix), and Joshi's 2024–25 Arithmetic Teichmüller preprints claim a proof without consensus. Best unconditional: Stewart–Yu log c≪R^{1/3}(log R)^3; Pasten 2024 subexponential under a≤c^{1−η}; Pasten Sept 2026: P(n²+1)≫(log₂n)²/log₄n.

title: Second moment of 3-torsion in imaginary quadratic class groups
W: Davenport–Heilbronn showed the average of |Cl(K)[3]| over imaginary quadratic fields is 2, as Cohen–Lenstra predicts. Cohen–Lenstra also predict the average of |Cl(K)[3]|² is 6. Prove this, or at least that the average is bounded.
M: Let $K$ range over imaginary quadratic fields with $|D_K|<X$. Cohen–Lenstra ($\mathbb E\,\#\mathrm{Sur}(\mathrm{Cl}_K,H)=1$ for $H=(\mathbb Z/3)^2$) predict $\frac{1}{\#\{K\}}\sum_K|\mathrm{Cl}_K[3]|^2\to 6$. Prove this limit, or prove $\sum_K|\mathrm{Cl}_K[3]|^2\ll X$.
why: This is the simplest odd-prime Cohen–Lenstra statement beyond Davenport–Heilbronn. It amounts to counting pairs of cubic fields with the same quadratic resolvent, i.e. certain degree-9 fields, which no parametrization handles. Smith's 2-primary breakthroughs do not reach odd ℓ because of the diagonal-entry problem for symmetric pairings.
status_notes: Known: first moment for ℓ=3 (Davenport–Heilbronn, Bhargava–Varma); full 2^∞ distribution for imaginary quadratics (Smith 2026); function-field large-q results (EVW, Landesman–Levy 2025). I did not find a proof of the ℓ=3 second moment; the 2026 survey arXiv 2606.06024 lists odd-ℓ control as open.

title: Lower the exponent 0.7785 for A4-quartic fields
W: Malle predicts about X^{1/2} log X quartic fields with Galois group A4 and discriminant up to X. Loughran–Paterson (2025) proved the matching lower bound. The best upper bound is still about X^{0.7785}. Lower the exponent.
M: Let $N_{A_4}(X)=\#\{L/\mathbb Q\ \text{quartic},\ \mathrm{Gal}=A_4,\ |\Delta_L|\le X\}$. Known: $X^{1/2}\log X\ll N_{A_4}(X)\ll X^{0.7785}$ (Loughran–Paterson 2025; Bhargava–Shankar–Taniguchi–Thorne–Tsimerman–Zhao, JAMS 2020, Thm 1.4). Prove $N_{A_4}(X)\ll X^{\beta}$ for some $\beta<0.778$, ideally $\beta=1/2+\varepsilon$.
why: A4 is the smallest group whose Malle count is open in both exponent and log-power. The upper bound reduces to bounding 2-torsion in class groups of cyclic cubic fields, so any gain is a gain on ℓ-torsion bounds, the bottleneck in most of Malle's conjecture. Since recent counterexamples hit Türkelli's refined b-constant, the cleanest unrefuted test case should be settled.
status_notes: Weak and strong Malle are open in general. Klüners' C3≀C2 counterexample to the b-constant is now asymptotically resolved (Alberts–Lemke Oliver–Wang–Wood, arXiv 2501.18574). Wang (2025) refuted Türkelli's modified b. A4: lower bound ≫X^{1/2}log X (Loughran–Paterson 2025), upper ≪X^{0.7785} (BSTTTZ 2020).

assumption: BSD + rank heuristics (minimalist / Goldfeld-type predictions for twist families)
title: Close the gap in the density of integers that are sums of two rational cubes
W: BSD plus the minimalist rank heuristic predict that exactly half of all integers are sums of two rational cubes. Proven: at least 2/21 are (Alpöge–Bhargava–Shnidman), and at least 31.95% are not (Koymans–Smith). Improve either bound.
M: Let $\mathcal S=\{n\in\mathbb Z: n=x^3+y^3,\ x,y\in\mathbb Q\}$ and $d_\pm$ the lower densities of $\mathcal S$ and of its complement (ordered by $|n|$). Known: $\underline d(\mathcal S)\ge 2/21$, $\underline d(\mathcal S^c)\ge 0.3195$. Conjecture: both densities equal $1/2$. Improve either constant.
why: This is a concrete, checkable stress test of the BSD-based rank heuristics on the cubic-twist family E_n: x³+y³=n. The 'not' side uses Selmer-group methods (rank 0), while the 'are' side needs rank ≥1 and so goes through Gross–Zagier/Kolyvagin or p-converse theorems. Root-number parity predicts exactly 1/2.
status_notes: ABS (2022) proved lower densities ≥2/21 (sums) and ≥1/6 (non-sums), confirming Davenport's conjecture. Koymans–Smith (2024) improved non-sums to ≥31.95% (per survey arXiv 2606.06024). Density 1/2 remains conjectural, resting on BSD plus minimalist rank conjectures.

assumption: Positive metric entropy / ergodicity of conservative systems (Sinai's standard-map conjecture)
title: Positive metric entropy of the Chirikov standard map at an explicit moderate parameter
W: Sinai conjectured that the standard map has positive metric entropy for every parameter k>0. After a 2026 AI-generated non-effective proof for large k, Slijepčević proved it for every k ≥ exp(2^{50000}). Bring the threshold down to a physically meaningful range, e.g. all k ≥ 10^6, or even a single explicit k ≤ 100.
M: Let $f_k(x,y)=(x+y+k\sin x,\ y+k\sin x)$ on $\mathbb T^2$ and $h_m(f_k)$ its metric entropy for Lebesgue measure. Known: $\log(2\pi k+4)-2^{430}\le h_m(f_k)$ for all $k\ge \exp(2^{50000})$ (Slijepčević 2026). Prove $h_m(f_k)>0$ for all $k\ge 10^{6}$, or for at least one explicit $k\le 100$.
why: This is the most famous instance of the Lyapunov/ergodicity assumption used throughout conservative dynamics and physics: positive exponents on a positive-measure set. The proof now exists for huge k, so the remaining gap is quantitative and well defined, and computer-assisted methods are plausible. Either success, or a mechanism showing the threshold cannot be lowered by these techniques, would be informative.
status_notes: Open for decades (Sinai, Herman). An OpenAI preprint (2026) proved positivity for all sufficiently large k (non-effective). Slijepčević (arXiv 2611.09361, Nov 2026) made it effective: h_m(f_k)=log k+O(1) for k≥exp(2^50000). Berger–Turaev (2019) proved Herman's positive-entropy conjecture for C^∞-perturbations.

assumption: Typicality of positive metric entropy for conservative surface dynamics (Palis/Herman-type typicality assumptions)
title: From density to Kolmogorov typicality of positive entropy in symplectic families
W: Berger and Turaev showed that families of area-preserving surface maps having positive metric entropy at every parameter are dense among smooth families. Show this is typical, i.e. holds for a Kolmogorov-generic (prevalent) set of families, or find a robust obstruction.
M: Let $\mathcal F$ be the space of $C^\infty$ $k$-parameter families $(f_p)_{p\in[0,1]^k}$ of symplectic diffeomorphisms of a surface having an elliptic periodic point. Berger–Turaev (2025, Thm B) show that families with $h_{\mathrm{Leb}}(f_p)>0$ for every $p$ are dense. Prove that for Kolmogorov-typical families in $\mathcal F$ (in their sense), $h_{\mathrm{Leb}}(f_p)>0$ for Lebesgue-a.e. $p$, or exhibit an open set of families where $\{p: h_{\mathrm{Leb}}(f_p)=0\}$ has positive measure.
why: Upgrading density to typicality is exactly what physicists implicitly assume when they treat chaotic Hamiltonian systems as ergodic. Berger–Turaev already have typicality for several other properties (periodic-point growth, universality, emergence), and positive entropy is the conspicuous gap.
status_notes: Herman's conjecture (C^∞-approximation by positive entropy) was proved by Berger–Turaev (2019). Their 2025 'Kolmogorov-typical properties of symplectic dynamics' gives typicality for super-exponential periodic growth, universality, and maximal emergence, but only density for everywhere-positive entropy (Thm B).

assumption: Stability of Gaussian elimination with pivoting (growth factor assumptions in numerical linear algebra)
title: Is the complete-pivoting growth factor superlinear?
W: Numerical analysts long assumed the worst-case growth factor of Gaussian elimination with complete pivoting is at most n. This was refuted: it is at least 1.0045n for n>10, and the limsup of g_n/n is at least 3.317. Decide whether g_n grows faster than every linear function, or better, like n^{1+δ}.
M: Let $g_n=\sup_A \max_{i,j,k}|a^{(k)}_{ij}|/\max_{ij}|a_{ij}|$ over real nonsingular $n\times n$ $A$ under complete pivoting. Known: $g_n\ge 1.0045n$ ($n>10$), $\limsup g_n/n\ge 3.317$ (Edelman–Urschel 2024), $g_n\le n^{0.2079\ln n+0.91}$ (Bisain–Edelman–Urschel 2024). Prove $g_n/n\to\infty$ along a subsequence, or $g_n\ge n^{1+\delta}$ infinitely often, or $g_n=O(n)$.
why: Complete pivoting is the textbook 'provably safe' variant of Gaussian elimination. The gap between linear lower bounds and a quasi-polynomial upper bound has stood since Wilkinson (1961), apart from one 2024 improvement. Superlinear growth would mean the classical stability folklore is false asymptotically, while O(n) would vindicate it.
status_notes: Folklore conjecture g_n≤n refuted for n>10 (Edelman–Urschel 2024, arXiv 2303.04892; Gould 1991 for n=13 in floating point). Their numerics give g_100>3n, and they suggest g_n/n→∞. Upper bound improved for the first time since Wilkinson: n^{0.2079 ln n+0.91} (arXiv 2312.00994).

assumption: Stability of Gaussian elimination with pivoting (growth factor assumptions in numerical linear algebra)
title: Is the complete-pivoting growth factor exactly 8 for 8x8 matrices?
W: The worst-case complete-pivoting growth is known exactly only for n ≤ 6 (values 1, 2, 2.25, 4, 4.1325, 5). The value g_8 = 8, attained by Hadamard matrices, is conjectured but unproven, and Hadamard matrices are known not to be optimal at n = 12 and 16. Determine g_7 and decide whether g_8 = 8.
M: With $g_n$ as above (real matrices, complete pivoting), prove or disprove $g_8=8$, and determine $g_7$ (known lower bounds from Edelman–Urschel Table 1).
why: This is a finite, computer-checkable test of the 'Hadamard is extremal' belief that underpinned the refuted g_n ≤ n conjecture. Edelman–Urschel note that the extremal matrix need not be Hadamard even when g_n = n, so n = 8 is where the structure first becomes unclear.
status_notes: Exact values: g_1..g_6=1,2,2.25,4,4.1325,5 (Day–Peterson, Gould, Edelman–Urschel). g_8=8 conjectured; g_12>12 and g_16>16 (Edelman–Urschel arXiv 2303.04892). Numerically g_n>n iff n≥11.

title: Optimal dimension dependence in the smoothed complexity of the simplex method
W: Bach and Huiberts (2025) found a simplex method with smoothed complexity O(σ^{-1/2} d^{11/4} log^{7/4} n) pivots and showed σ^{-1/2} is optimal. In the dimension d, the best lower bound is only about d^{1/2}. Close the gap in d.
M: Let $S(d,n,\sigma)$ be the best smoothed complexity (expected pivot count, worst over unit-norm data perturbed by $N(0,\sigma^2)$) of any simplex method on LPs with $d$ variables and $n$ constraints. Known: $S\ll\sigma^{-1/2}d^{11/4}\log^{7/4}n$, and a diameter lower bound $\Omega(\sigma^{-1/2}d^{1/2}\ln(4/\sigma)^{-1/4})$ at $n=\lfloor(4/\sigma)^d\rfloor$ (Bach–Huiberts 2025). Determine the exponent of $d$: improve $11/4$ or prove a lower bound $d^{\beta}$ with $\beta>1/2$.
why: Smoothed analysis is the standard explanation for why the simplex method works in practice. With σ-dependence now optimal, the d exponent is the remaining question of whether the explanation is quantitatively sharp. A matching lower bound would come from new constructions of smoothed polytopes with long shadow paths.
status_notes: Spielman–Teng (2004) first bound; Huiberts–Lee–Zhang (STOC 2023) O(σ^{-3/2}d^{13/4}log^{7/4}n); Bach–Huiberts (arXiv 2504.04197, 2025) O(σ^{-1/2}d^{11/4}log^{7/4}n), σ-optimal up to polylogs, d gap open.

assumption: Polynomial Hirsch conjecture (diameter assumption behind simplex-method efficiency)
title: Beat the (1-o(1)) log2 d exponent in quasi-polynomial polytope diameter bounds
W: All known bounds on the diameter of a d-dimensional polyhedron with n facets have the form (n−d)^{log₂ d − O(log log d)}. The latest (Liu–Ge–Ye 2026) is (n−d)^{log₂ G_d} with G_d ~ (4 ln 2) d/(ln d)². Get an exponent at most (1−ε) log₂ d.
M: Let $\Delta_u(d,n)$ be the maximum graph diameter of a pointed $d$-polyhedron with $n$ facets. Known: $\Delta_u(d,n)\le (n-d)^{\log_2 G_d}$, $G_d=(4\ln2+o(1))d/(\ln d)^2$ (Liu–Ge–Ye 2026), after Kalai–Kleitman, Todd, Sukegawa. Prove $\Delta_u(d,n)\le (n-d)^{(1-\varepsilon)\log_2 d}$ for some fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and all large $d$.
why: Every improvement since 1992 has shaved only lower-order terms off the Kalai–Kleitman exponent, and Liu–Ge–Ye argue their leading term is sharp for path-counting recursions. A constant-factor gain in the exponent would therefore need a structurally new argument, which is a meaningful step toward the polynomial Hirsch conjecture.
status_notes: Hirsch refuted (Santos 2012); polynomial Hirsch open. Bounds: Kalai–Kleitman n^{2+log₂d}, Todd (n−d)^{log₂d}, Sukegawa (n−d)^{log₂(d/ln d)+O(1)}, Liu–Ge–Ye 2026 (arXiv 2609.33434) exponent log₂(c d/ln²d), plus excess bound (n−d)^{½log₂(n−d)+O(1)}.
